_note: The Gym manifest (WP25a): which grammar points act as selectable form categories, grouped into picker columns. 'point' must match the grammar point title exactly (resolved to ids at request time). 'usage' is the plain-language hover explanation; 'example' is a short illustration. 'nonstandard': forms hidden behind the 'include non-standard words' toggle.

entries.point: Simple present: करता हूँ, करती है, करते हैं
entries.label: Simple present
entries.usage: Habitual present, agreeing with gender.
entries.example: मैं हिंदी बोलता हूँ।

entries.point: Present continuous: रहा है, रही है, रहे हैं
entries.label: Present continuous
entries.usage: Happening right now.
entries.example: मैं खा रहा हूँ।

entries.label: Simple past
entries.usage: A finished past action.
entries.example: वह घर गया।

entries.label: Future
entries.usage: What will happen.
entries.example: मैं कल आऊँगा।

entries.point: The perfect tenses: चुका है, गया था
entries.label: Perfect tenses
entries.usage: Completed action with relevance.

entries.point: Let's and may I: the subjunctive
entries.label: Subjunctive
entries.usage: Wish, suggestion, possibility.
entries.example: शायद वह आए।

entries.point: The ergative ने: मैंने किताब पढ़ी
entries.label: Ergative ने
entries.usage: Past transitive: subject takes ने.
entries.example: मैंने किताब पढ़ी।

entries.label: Causatives
entries.usage: make / have someone do.
entries.example: मैंने खाना बनवाया।

entries.label: Word order
entries.usage: Where the words go: the verb comes last.
entries.example: मैं चाय पीता हूँ। — I drink tea.

entries.point: The verb 'to be': हूँ, है, हो, हैं
entries.label: To be हूँ/है/हैं
entries.usage: Am, is, are — Hindi never leaves it out.
entries.example: मैं डॉक्टर हूँ। — I am a doctor.

entries.label: Negation
entries.usage: Saying you don't do something, or telling someone not to.
entries.example: मैं कॉफ़ी नहीं पीता। — I don't drink coffee.

entries.point: Questions: क्या and the question words
entries.label: Questions
entries.usage: Asking yes-or-no, or what, who, where and when.
entries.example: क्या आप भारत से हैं? — Are you from India?

entries.label: Commands
entries.usage: Telling or asking someone to do something.
entries.example: यहाँ बैठो। (to a friend) — Sit here. (informal)

entries.point: Past 'to be': था, थी, थे, थीं
entries.label: Past था/थी/थे
entries.usage: Was and were, matching who you are talking about.
entries.example: कल मैं घर पर था। (a man speaking) — Yesterday I was at home. (male)

entries.point: Wanting and needing: चाहिए and चाहना
entries.label: Wanting चाहिए
entries.usage: Saying you want or need something.
entries.example: मुझे एक कप चाय चाहिए। — I want a cup of tea.

entries.label: Can सकना
entries.usage: Saying what you are able to do.
entries.example: मैं हिंदी बोल सकता हूँ। (a man speaking) — I can speak Hindi. (male)

entries.point: Compound verbs: ले जाना, खा लेना
entries.label: Compound verbs
entries.usage: Finishing an action off — eaten up, given away, fallen asleep.
entries.example: मैंने पूरा खाना खा लिया। — I ate up all the food.

entries.label: Necessity
entries.usage: Should, have to, or had no choice.
entries.example: तुम्हें डॉक्टर के पास जाना चाहिए। — You should go to the doctor.

entries.label: Relative जो… वह
entries.usage: Saying 'the one who…' with a matching pair of words.
entries.example: जो मेहनत करता है, वह सफल होता है। — The one who works hard succeeds.

entries.label: Conditionals
entries.usage: If this happens, then that — real or imaginary.
entries.example: अगर तुम पढ़ोगे तो पास हो जाओगे। — If you study, you'll pass.

entries.label: Passive
entries.usage: When what happened matters more than who did it.
entries.example: भारत में कई भाषाएँ बोली जाती हैं। — Many languages are spoken in India.

entries.label: Presumptive होगा
entries.usage: Guessing what is probably true right now.
entries.example: अभी दस बजे हैं, वह दफ़्तर में होगा। — It's ten now; he must be at the office.

entries.point: Aspect verbs: लगना, रहना, चुकना, जाना
entries.label: Start, keep, finish
entries.usage: An action beginning, carrying on, or already over.
entries.example: बच्चा अचानक रोने लगा। — The child suddenly began to cry.

entries.label: Reported speech
entries.usage: Telling someone what another person said.
entries.example: उसने कहा कि वह कल आएगा। — He said that he would come tomorrow.

entries.label: Participles हुए
entries.usage: Doing one thing while doing another.
entries.example: घर आते हुए मैंने बाज़ार देखा। — While coming home, I saw the market.

entries.point: Ne-construction edge cases and split ergativity
entries.label: ने exceptions
entries.usage: Which past sentences take ने — and which verbs never do.
entries.example: मैं कल बाज़ार से फल लाया। — I brought fruit from the market yesterday. (male)

entries.point: The oblique case: कमरे में, लड़के को
entries.label: Oblique case
entries.usage: Noun form before a postposition.
entries.example: लड़का → लड़के को

entries.label: Postpositions
entries.usage: in / on / from / to — after the noun.
entries.example: घर में, मेज़ पर

entries.label: Plurals
entries.usage: Noun plural by gender.
entries.example: किताब → किताबें

entries.label: Possession का/के/की
entries.usage: 's — agrees with the thing owned.
entries.example: राम का घर, राम की किताब

entries.label: Gender
entries.usage: Every noun is masculine or feminine.
entries.example: लड़का (m), लड़की (f)

entries.point: Pronouns and politeness: तू, तुम, आप
entries.label: Pronouns तू/तुम/आप
entries.usage: Picking the right 'you' for the person you are talking to.
entries.example: आप कैसे हैं? — How are you? (respectful)

entries.point: Having things: के पास, का, को
entries.label: I have के पास
entries.usage: Saying you have something — a bike, a brother, a fever.
entries.example: मेरे पास एक साइकिल है। — I have a bicycle.

entries.label: Comparison
entries.usage: Saying one thing is bigger than another, or the best of all.
entries.example: हाथी घोड़े से बड़ा है। — An elephant is bigger than a horse.

entries.point: Adverbs and manner: से, कर के, तरह
entries.label: Adverbs
entries.usage: Saying how something is done — quickly, carefully, calmly.
entries.example: कृपया ध्यान से सुनिए। — Please listen attentively.

entries.point: Experiencer subjects: मुझे लगता है, पसंद है
entries.label: Feelings मुझे
entries.usage: Liking, feeling and thinking, where 'I' becomes मुझे.
entries.example: मुझे यह गाना पसंद है। — I like this song.

entries.label: Numbers
entries.usage: Counting things, and saying first, second, half.
entries.example: यह मेरा पहला बच्चा है। — This is my first child.

entries.point: Register: तत्सम Sanskrit vs Perso-Arabic vocabulary
entries.label: Register
entries.usage: Choosing the formal word or the everyday one.
entries.example: आपकी मदद के लिए बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद। — Thank you very much for your help. (formal; among friends: शुक्रिया)

entries.label: Honorific plural
entries.usage: Speaking of one respected person as if they were several.
entries.example: पिताजी अभी घर आए हैं। — Father has just come home. (honorific plural)

entries.label: Idioms मन/दिल
entries.usage: Everyday phrases built on मन (mind) and दिल (heart).
entries.example: आज मेरा घूमने का मन कर रहा है। — I feel like going out today.

entries.point: Discourse particles: तो, ही, भी, न, वाला
entries.label: Particles तो/ही/भी
entries.usage: Small words that add only, even, or 'as for me'.
entries.example: मैं तो यह काम आज ही करूँगा। — As for me, I'll do this very task today.

entries.point: Literary and poetic syntax: inversion, ellipsis, Urdu izafat
entries.label: Izafat & inversion
entries.usage: Reading poetry and old-fashioned writing, where the words arrive in an unexpected order.
entries.example: शमा-ए-महफ़िल देर रात तक जलती रही। — The candle of the gathering burned on late into the night.
